job.title: Manager Communities & Cultural Services
job.description:
Manager Community & Cultural Services
Central Highlands Regional Council | Emerald, QLD | $210K–$252K TRP
  
Public Sector People is partnering with Central Highlands Regional Council to appoint a Manager Community & Cultural Services, an influential leadership role based in Emerald.
  
An opportunity to lead, influence and make a difference.
  
Take ownership of a broad portfolio of services that matter to communities across the Central Highlands, with the freedom to develop people, strengthen performance and shape future priorities.
  
Council is seeking a confident, practical leader who can bring teams together, solve complex problems and turn strategic direction into tangible results.
  
With key initiatives underway, you will build on established foundations, strengthen governance and capability, and make a lasting contribution to the organisation and its communities.
  
The Opportunity
  
Reporting to the Director Communities, you will lead libraries, arts and culture, community grants, regional events, youth programs, First Nations initiatives, community relationships and human and social recovery.
  
This varied portfolio calls for a leader who can connect different functions, set clear priorities and deliver outcomes. You do not need to be a technical specialist in every service area; strong leadership and good governance are essential.
  
Your key responsibilities will include:
  • Providing strategic and operational leadership across the Community and Cultural Services portfolio
  • Coaching and developing multidisciplinary teams and strengthening accountability and performance
  • Improving the quality and effectiveness of community programs and public-facing services
  • Progressing strategies and initiatives across libraries, arts, culture and heritage
  • Overseeing community grants and aligning programs with Council and community priorities
  • Managing budgets, resources, service performance and financial accountability
  • Building partnerships with community organisations, Traditional Owners and government agencies
  • Providing considered advice to the Executive Leadership Team and elected representatives
  • Strengthening governance, systems, planning and operational processes
  • Identifying practical opportunities for innovation and measurable community outcomes
About You
  
Above all, you will be a capable people leader who gets results.
  
You will thrive in a complex service environment, communicate clearly, navigate competing priorities and bring people with you through change while setting high expectations.
  
Ideally, you will bring:
  
  • Proven leadership experience in government, community services or a complex service organisation
  • Experience managing multidisciplinary teams and building capability in others
  • Good governance, financial management and operational planning skills
  • Ability to translate strategy into practical programs and measurable outcomes
  • Strong communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement capability
  • Confidence working with executives, elected representatives and diverse communities
  • Sound judgement and an ability to manage competing expectations and priorities
  • Experience delivering positive community outcomes and service improvements
  • A collaborative, practical approach to change and continuous improvement
  • Relevant tertiary qualifications and/or substantial comparable leadership experience
Council welcomes candidates from local and state government, major not-for-profit organisations and other community-focused service providers. A traditional community services background is not essential if you can demonstrate effective leadership and accountable service delivery.
  
This may also suit an experienced Coordinator or senior leader from a larger organisation who is ready to step into broader management responsibility.
  
Why Central Highlands Regional Council?
  
This is your opportunity to influence more than day-to-day operations: shape a diverse portfolio and the way services evolve across the region.
  
Council is progressing initiatives across libraries, arts, youth, heritage, events and community grants. You will build on this work, strengthen your team and improve the experience of the communities Council serves.
You will have room to introduce fresh ideas while working within a supportive and accountable local government environment.
  
For a leader motivated by variety, problem-solving and community impact, this is an opportunity to make the role your own.
  
The opportunity offers:
  • $210,000–$252,000 Total Remuneration Package
  • A visible senior leadership role across a broad and varied portfolio
  • Relocation assistance for candidates moving to the region
  • Potential access to Council accommodation
Based in Emerald, you can enjoy the benefits of regional living, a welcoming community and access to the Central Highlands’ remarkable natural attractions.
If you are ready to develop people, improve services and contribute to the future of the Central Highlands, we would welcome a confidential discussion.
  
Be part of something that matters, with like-minded people who truly care. One Place. Many Paths. Choose Yours Here.

The Facilities Manager is responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance and presentation of a high-profile, 27-storey mixed-use residential building in Perth CBD, comprising 219 apartments across social housing, affordable housing and SDA.

Reporting to the Manager, Corporate Assets, you will take ownership of onsite facilities operations, working closely with the wider WA Property Services team to coordinate maintenance, manage contractors and ensure building services and infrastructure operate safely, efficiently and in line with relevant compliance requirements.

With the building preparing to open, this is an opportunity to be involved from the early stages, commencing approximately six weeks before opening to help establish maintenance processes, coordinate contractors and ensure the building is operationally ready.

The role offers a broad mix of responsibilities across building infrastructure, preventative and responsive maintenance, defect management, inspections and upgrades. You will oversee contractor performance across essential services, monitor compliance, maintain asset and maintenance records, manage operating expenditure and respond to issues as they arise.

You will also work closely with Housing Officers and the Allocations team to coordinate repairs and maintenance across individual dwellings, including vacate inspections, while helping maintain a positive experience for residents.

This is a hands on, site-based opportunity for someone who enjoys taking ownership, solving practical problems and ensuring a building is maintained to a high standard. You will have the autonomy to manage day-to-day operations while working collaboratively with an established property team.

About You
You are an experienced facilities or property professional with a strong understanding of building infrastructure, maintenance and contractor management. You enjoy being close to the operational side of a building and are confident coordinating competing priorities in a live residential environment.

You bring experience managing preventative and reactive maintenance, overseeing contractors and service providers, identifying defects and ensuring issues are followed through to resolution. You understand the importance of building compliance, workplace health and safety and maintaining accurate asset and maintenance records.

You will be organised, proactive and comfortable working autonomously, with the communication skills to build effective relationships with contractors, internal stakeholders and residents. You can manage day-to-day operational challenges while maintaining a strong focus on safety, service delivery and building presentation.

Residential apartment or mixed use building experience will be highly regarded, as will exposure to social housing, affordable housing, SDA or other residential environments supporting people with diverse needs. 

This role would strongly suit:
  • A Facilities Manager with experience managing high-density residential apartment buildings or mixed-use developments.

  • A building operations professional with a strong understanding of essential services, compliance and preventative maintenance.
  • A facilities or property professional from a community housing, affordable housing, SDA or other residential environment looking to take ownership of a significant building.
Relevant qualifications in facilities management, building services, property, engineering, a trade or a related discipline are desirable. A current driver's licence is required, along with the ability to complete relevant employment screening checks.

The Opportunity
This is an opportunity to take ownership of facilities operations within a significant residential building, playing a key role in preparing the asset for opening and establishing effective day-to-day maintenance and contractor management processes.

You will join a collaborative property team and contribute to maintaining a safe, functional and welcoming environment for residents across a diverse mixed tenure housing model.
